notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2023, as the village reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Kalamazoo County and the township the village is part of.
Village residents also pay the township the village is part of, which is listed separately.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Michigan local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Michigan yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
